**Setup.** Stations 1–14. A passenger trip (A,B), A<B, occupies one unit of capacity on every edge (i,i+1) for A≤i<B. The bus load on edge (i,i+1) is the number of passengers whose interval covers that edge; it must be ≤ 25. A pair (A,B) is *used* if ≥1 passenger has that trip; otherwise *unused*. Let G be the graph on {1,…,14} whose edges are the unused pairs. We seek N = min over feasible configs of ν(G) (max matching of G).

---

**Upper bound: N ≤ 4 (a feasible config with ν(G)=4).**

Use exactly one passenger on every pair (A,B) with 1≤A<B≤10 (45 passengers, all trips within {1,…,10}). Load on edge (i,i+1) for 1≤i≤9 is i(10−i): 9,16,21,24,**25**,24,21,16,9 — max 25 ≤ C. Loads on edges 10,11,12,13 are 0. Feasible.

Unused pairs are exactly those with at least one endpoint in {11,12,13,14}. So {1,…,10} is an independent set in G, while {11,12,13,14} is a clique with all cross-edges to {1,…,10}. Every edge of G touches {11,12,13,14}, which has only 4 vertices, so ν(G) ≤ 4; and matching (1,11),(2,12),(3,13),(4,14) gives ν(G)=4. Hence **N ≤ 4**.

---

**Lower bound: N ≥ 4 (every feasible config has ν(G) ≥ 4).**

Suppose for contradiction some feasible config has ν(G) ≤ 3. By the **Tutte–Berge theorem**,
ν(G) = ½·min_{U⊆V}(|V|+|U|−o(G−U)), equivalently ν(G)=(14−def)/2 with def = max_U(o(G−U)−|U|).
ν(G)≤3 forces def ≥ 8, so there exists U with o(G−U)−|U| ≥ 8. Since o(G−U) ≤ 14−|U|, we get |U|+8 ≤ 14−|U|, i.e. **|U| ≤ 3**.

Let the components of G−U be C₁,…,Cₖ. Any pair joining two different components is **not** an edge of G, hence is **used**. Therefore the bus load on every edge is at least the number of cross-component pairs covering it. We show this forced load exceeds 25 in every case.

A useful fact: if W = V\U has |W| = n′ stations, then as i runs from 1 to 13, the count (#W ≤ i) increases from 0 to n′ (stepping by 0 or 1), so it attains every integer value, in particular ⌊n′/2⌋. At the edge i where #W≤i = ⌊n′/2⌋, the number of cross-component pairs covering edge i equals
(#W≤i)(#W>i) − Σⱼ pⱼqⱼ,
where pⱼ+qⱼ = |Cⱼ| are the splits of component Cⱼ across edge i. We bound this from below in each case (adversary chooses the partition minimizing the load, i.e. maximizing within-component crossing Σpⱼqⱼ subject to o ≥ |U|+8 odd components).

**|U|=3, n′=11.** Need o ≥ 11, so all 11 components are singletons. All C(11,2)=55 pairs used. Forced load at #W=5: 5·6 = **30 > 25**. ✗

**|U|=2, n′=12.** Need o ≥ 10. The partition maximizing within-component pairs is 9 singletons + 1 triple (within-pairs = 3; a "10 singletons + 1 pair" option gives only 1). At #W=6: forced load ≥ 6·6 − 2 = **34 > 25** (a triple contributes at most ⌊9/4⌋=2 crossing pairs at any edge). ✗

**|U|=1, n′=13.** Need o ≥ 9. Best partition: 8 singletons + 1 component of size 5 (within-pairs = 10; alternatives 7 sing+2 triples give 6, 9 sing+2 pairs give 2). At #W=6: forced load ≥ 6·7 − 6 = **36 > 25** (size-5 component contributes at most ⌊25/4⌋=6). ✗

**|U|=0, n′=14.** Need o ≥ 8. Best partition: 7 singletons + 1 component of size 7 (within-pairs = 21; alternatives 8 sing+1 six give 15, 6 sing+1 triple+1 five give 13). At #W=7: forced load ≥ 7·7 − 12 = **37 > 25** (size-7 component contributes at most ⌊49/4⌋=12). ✗

(For |U|=0, concentrating mass into one straddling size-7 component maximizes Σpⱼqⱼ at the middle edge; any split into smaller components yields smaller crossing and hence larger load — verified by the convexity of p·q: e.g. 8 singletons + size-6 gives load ≥ 40, 6 singletons + 2 triples + 1 pair gives ≥ 44.)

In every case the forced load on some edge strictly exceeds C = 25, contradicting feasibility. Therefore no feasible configuration can have ν(G) ≤ 3; i.e. **ν(G) ≥ 4 always**, so **N ≥ 4**.

---

**Conclusion.** N ≤ 4 and N ≥ 4, so

$$N = \boxed{4}.$$
